merger_name: KKR – global print business of Thomson Reuters Corporation
merger_description:
Thomson Reuters Corporation (via its wholly owned subsidiaries, Thomson Reuters Holdco LLC and West Publishing Corporation) will transfer assets comprising its global print business (the **Target Business**) to Omni JV LLC, a Delaware limited liability company. Following this transfer, MCNLST LLC, a special purpose vehicle indirectly majority owned by insurance vehicles and accounts managed by various subsidiaries of KKR & Co. Inc., New York, United States (together with its subsidiaries, **KKR**), will purchase all of the Class A Membership Units of Omni JV LLC, which represent 51% of the outstanding Membership Units of Omni JV LLC (the **Acquisition**).

As a result of the Acquisition, KKR, via MCNLST LLC, will acquire 51% of the capital and voting rights in Omni JV LLC. Entities owned by Thomson Reuters Corporation will hold the remaining 49% of the membership units in Omni JV LLC.

KKR is a global investment firm that offers alternative asset management as well as capital markets and insurance solutions. KKR sponsors investment funds that invest in private equity, credit, and real assets and has strategic partners that manage hedge funds.

Thomson Reuters Corporation is a global content and technology company, which operates across five business areas: Legal Professionals, Corporates, Tax, Audit and Accounting Professionals, Reuters, and Global Print.

The Target Business operates a scaled printing, publishing, fulfilment, and distribution business serving legal, tax, accounting, governmental, corporate, and institutional customers in the United States and internationally.

events.title: Notification waiver determination published

determination_table_content.details:
In making this notification waiver determination, the Australian
Competition and Consumer Commission (the ACCC) has considered
the information provided with the notification waiver application and
had regard to the factors in section 51ABV(2)(b) of the Competition
and Consumer Act 2010 (Cth) (the Act).
Based on the information currently before it, the ACCC considers that
the Acquisition is unlikely to give rise to any material lessening of
competition given:
a. there is no or limited horizontal overlap between KKR (including
its connected entities) and the Target Business in the publishing
and supply of legal and tax professional content in Australia
b. there is no vertical relationship between the parties (including
their connected entities) in Australia.
In these circumstances, the ACCC does not consider it necessary to
reach a concluded view on the likelihood of the notification
thresholds being met.
Given that material competition concerns are unlikely to arise, the
ACCC has determined that the Acquisition is not required to be
notified.
The ACCC considers that the determination is consistent with the
object of the Act and the interests of consumers in promoting
competition.
For more information about the ACCC’s approach to considering
notification waiver applications and to assessing competition
effects more generally, see the ACCC’s guidance on notification
waivers and merger assessment guidelines.
